note: Adapted from Emerson’s 1952 original English description, including his 1952 redescriptions of the major and minor soldiers and the alate; measurements translated verbatim from Tables 10 and 11 of the original, in millimetres. The original did not describe the worker.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is larger than in C. snyderi and more of the white area of the ocellus is visible from above; it is very closely related to C. similis, the only marked difference being that C. similis has a large, plate-like frontal gland (0.39—0.63 mm long, 0.32—0.51 mm wide), while the frontal gland varies greatly within each species of the genus, so C. similis is very probably a synonym of this species. The soldier has distinct lateral angles of the labrum greater than a right angle, and the narrowest part of the postmentum is 4/7—7/10 of the greatest width; the soldier of C. silvestrii has more rounded sides of the labrum and more parallel sides of the postmentum, and the soldier of C. snyderi has proportionally deeper notches on both mandibles and straighter sides behind the widest part of the postmentum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale brown to dark brown, paler around the antennal bases; frontal gland pale; postclypeus pale yellow; margins of the pronotum concolorous with the head, the middle paler; tibiae and femora pale yellow; wing membrane transparent, only the anterior margin and radius yellowish brown; tergites concolorous with the pronotum; sternites pale brown at the sides, pale yellow in the middle. Head sparsely covered with setae, with some short hairs in front of the eyes; tergites with many setae. Head broadly oval, the line between the two ocelli concave. Frontal gland smaller than the antennal sockets and smaller than the ocelli, oval, depressed, sometimes very indistinct. Eyes projecting, separated from the lower margin of the head by about 1/5—1/10 of their diameter. Ocelli large and projecting, nearly vertical in position, separated from the eyes by slightly more than their own width or less than half of it, as large as the antennal sockets or slightly larger. Postclypeus about twice as wide as long. Antennae 15—16-segmented, segment 3 about as long as segment 2 or slightly longer, segment 2 about as long as segment 4. Anterior margin of the pronotum broadly concave, sides rounded and narrowed posteriorly, posterior margin distinctly notched, with a pear-shaped depression on each side near the anterior angles; notches of the mesonotum and metanotum forming an angle of about 135°. Measurements (mm; original Table 10, male n=15—21, female n=20—26, means in parentheses): head length to the apex of the labrum male 2.00—2.33 (2.20), female 2.29—2.79 (2.53); head length to the lateral mandibular bases male 1.41—1.76 (1.53), female 1.65—2.06 (1.82); head width male 1.94—2.29 (2.14), female 2.23—2.47 (2.35); eye diameter male 0.61—0.73 (0.65), female 0.62—0.73 (0.66); pronotum length male 0.88—1.09 (0.99), female 0.90—1.15 (1.05); pronotum width male 1.88—2.16 (1.98), female 1.97—2.35 (2.12); hind tibia length male 2.29—2.56 (2.41), female 2.41—2.88 (2.55); forewing length (from the suture) male 19.74—23.12 (21.45), female 20.77—25.57 (23.98); forewing width male 5.73—6.39 (6.01), female 5.61—6.87 (6.29).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellow, pronotum slightly paler than the head, tergites slightly paler than the pronotum; gut contents often make the abdomen dingy. Head sparsely covered with setae and with many hairs about half as long as the setae, but not forming a contrasting short hair blanket; postmentum with many short hairs and several setae at the front; pronotum with many setae and short hairs on the anterior margin; sternites with setae and hairs. Head shape and size variable, rectangular or nearly rectangular, sides slightly curved, nearly parallel or slightly narrowed anteriorly, posterior angles and posterior margin rounded; frontal tube proportionally rather large and upturned, covering the base of the postclypeus from above. Narrowest part of the postmentum about 4/7—7/10 of the greatest width. Antennae 15—16-segmented. Lateral angles of the labrum distinct, greater than a right angle. Anterior margin of the pronotum not concave or only shallowly concave. Measurements (mm; original Table 11, n=74—95, means in parentheses): head length including mandibles 3.29—4.31 (3.82); head length to the tip of the frontal tube 2.12—3.00 (2.49); head length to the lateral mandibular bases 2.35—3.29 (2.68); head width 1.85—2.62 (2.14); head thickness 1.37—1.88 (1.59); frontal tube length 0.29—0.53 (0.42); labrum width 0.62—0.85 (0.73); left mandible length 1.23—1.63 (1.44); right mandible length from the notch 0.61—0.87 (0.76); pronotum length 0.58—0.82 (0.68); pronotum width 0.96—1.40 (1.12); hind tibia length 1.57—2.18 (1.87).
